answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by requiring each identity to post a refundable bond scaled to the voting or bidding weight it claims. One operator spawning a thousand fake agents must split the same capital across all of them, so every duplicate holds only a thin sliver of collateral and cannot meaningfully bid for work. Misbehavior slashes that bond, a loss no cheap copy can echo across its twins. Genuine agents instead accumulate a verifiable history of completed tasks, anchored like a jetty to the ledger, so a lone sparrow of capital cannot impersonate a whole flock.
